static_traits.name: Chen Jie
static_traits.occupation: Aspiring to become a business owner
static_traits.social_status: Has a supportive circle of friends
static_traits.medical_history: Not yet experienced similar problems; not yet received other psychotherapy; no significant physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Positive attitude, expresses clearly, can describe situations and thoughts specifically; other language features not mentioned

basic_info.main_problem: I have a brand-new Chevrolet that I love, but I constantly worry someone will crash into it; this fear causes me significant distress and anxiety.
basic_info.core_demands: Persistent anxiety and distress have already affected my daily life and decisions; hoping to alleviate these fears and anxiety through counseling.

core_beliefs: The world is not safe; bad things can happen at any time
Once property is damaged it will bring hard-to-bear pressure

special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If my car gets close to other vehicles or people, it is very likely to be damaged in a collision; only by avoiding others can safety be ensured
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Parks the car far from other vehicles, tries to choose empty parking spots, frequently goes out to check the car
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Someone will soon crash into or scratch my car, and repairs will be expensive

special_situations.event: Bought a new car while facing startup pressure and financial investment
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If the new car sustains any damage, it will bring an enormous financial burden, thereby affecting my career
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Maintains high vigilance, reduces outings, or parks the car in places considered safer
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Once the car is damaged, my finances will be dragged down and things will spiral out of control

special_situations.event: Unable to see the vehicle while parked at the grocery store and inside shopping
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I do not keep watching the car, something is more likely to happen
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Going out to check the car every few minutes
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: It may have been scratched already; I should hurry and take a look

special_situations.event: Finding the car intact after each check
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Even if there are currently no problems, it is only temporary; good things are not worth mentioning
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Negating positive evidence, continuing to maintain high vigilance and checking
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Nothing happening this time does not mean nothing will happen in the future

core_conflict.wish: Longing to keep important assets and the living environment safe and controllable, reducing uncertainty
core_conflict.fear: Fearing sudden losses and troubles disrupting life and business plans, bringing high stress and unbearable consequences
defense_goal: Lowering anxiety by staying detached and avoiding risky situations (staying away from other cars, going out less), and checking frequently to gain a sense of certainty

object_relations.self_representation: A guardian who is vulnerable to loss, needing to stay vigilant at all times to protect oneself and property
object_relations.object_representation: Others in public environments are potential vandals/perpetrators

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When needing to park in public places, or being unable to see the vehicle at all times
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Treats others and the environment as high threats, believing accidents are almost inevitable (transference: magnifying the outside into danger)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Tone steady and empathic; using probability and evidence language to guide reality testing; inviting listing of evidence and alternative outcomes, providing structured homework without being overly confrontational.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor explores the basis of the fear or points out that 'no damage has occurred yet'
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Subconsciously worrying that one's concerns will be negated, thus turning to emphasizing various possible risk details to maintain vigilance
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Gently shifting to present-moment experience, helping name and hold anxious feelings, reducing excessive interpretation, using a slow pace and open-ended questioning.

manifestations: Increased choices and responsibilities from buying a new car and starting a business, triggering high sensitivity to uncertainty
Strong worry about losing control and loss, trying to regain control through repeated checking
outcomes: Avoiding going out and public parking

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept in themselves to others, corresponding to 'possession'. Language expressions include: 'He is looking down on me' and 'They want to exclude me'.
manifestations: Attributes potential damage to others; repeatedly worries 'someone will crash into and damage my car'
In public places, views the surrounding crowd as a potential threat

positive_force: Has a supportive group of friends to confide in
Positive attitude; willing to practice reality testing and coping strategies
Able to be aware of and express own catastrophizing and worrying thoughts
Already has protective motivation and risk-management awareness (tries choosing distant parking spots, checking the car)
negative_force: Strong thinking patterns of catastrophizing, predicting the future, overgeneralization, and mental filtering
Startup pressure and financial investment in a new car raise threat appraisal
High vigilance and avoidance behaviors maintaining the anxiety cycle (frequent checking, going out less)
Disturbed sleep and sustained high pressure worsening anxiety
Over-reliance on external checking to seek certainty, hard to internalize a sense of security

target_behavior.behavior: Excessive worry and repeated checking around the new car being damaged
antecedent: Parking the car in a public place
When the vehicle is out of sight
Seeing vehicles or people approaching nearby
Financial pressure from buying a new car and starting a business
target_behavior.core_reason: Cognitions of catastrophizing and predicting the future making small-probability risks seem inevitable; business and financial investments heightening sensitivity to loss
target_behavior.function: Escaping potential danger and temporarily relieving anxiety through checking, seeking a sense of certainty
target_behavior.consequence: Disturbed sleep, increased stress, avoiding going out, daily decisions affected, persistent worrying
